svg.title: Anna's Git Architecture
svg.desc: Local computers and private working repository are deliberately compared. An audited approval generates adjusted publication data without private work history. Public publication repository and agreed archive handover are separate functions; website, consulting and persistent identifiers require their own institution or agreement.

g.title: Anna edits her edition files on her computer. In the preferred way, she uses a prepared oXygen author environment, TEI-schema, Git connection and local preview. The markdown path uses text editor, documented conventions and appropriate checks. Changes are only saved outside of this computer when they have been transferred to the agreed external repo.
g.text: oXygen Author · Git client · TEI files · local validation
Local preview and documented edition principles

g.title: The working repository keeps the recorded files and their Git history ready for the agreed reading circle. Regular commits and pushes to a reliable operated service can secure the edition files against computer loss. Advice is its own performance; it does not follow solely from a GitLab access. Internal XML comments can be retained in older working positions.
g.text: Comparison · Git-History · Consulting as agreed additional service
Internal working versions and communication remain in the appropriate reading circle

g.title: This is a work step, not an additional storage location. Anna selects a verified version, clears rights and metadata, removes internal working notes and documents posts as well as share scope. She exports the shared files without the private Git history. A suitable output path creates HTML or PDF if required; raw TEI will not be created by itself to the finished website.
g.text: TEI check · editorial approval · Check rights and metadata
Adjusted export · if necessary transformation to HTML / PDF

g.title: The own publication repository contains only deliberately released data, edition principles, metadata, terms of use and designated release states. It can be located on the same or another hosting service than the working repository. An additional static reading view can be provided via GitHub Pages, for example, when the output path is set up. The private working repository is not simply switched publicly.
g.text: Released data · Releases · optional read view
e.g. on GitHub · same or other host possible

g.title: A suitable archive service takes over a defined data status and metadata according to an agreement. Long-term responsibility, access conditions and a persistent identifier – for example DOI – are clarified separately. Git hosting neither automatically creates an archive nor automatically creates a DOI. Which work history may be kept separately is its own decision.
g.text: Persistent identifier, e.g. DOI, by agreement
Expenditure is planned under a approval, not services already provided.
Independent backup complements the repo reconciliation. Git hosting, consulting and archiving are our own tasks.
Editionskompass · Anna · preferred starting model with TEI and institutional GitLab · October 20, 2026
